about: What a correct lens proposes on the Pebble Shop fixture (seeded, must: true) and what it must not (decoy: true). Scored by skill/scripts/lib/score.mjs: an emitted card is assigned to the one item its anchors land on most strongly (`anchor` is the primary, `also` the other files a correct card may anchor on; `also` may name a file the finding says is missing). Hypotheses are the H-numbers of each pack at lens_version 0.1.0. Primary anchors are unique within a lens. At most 4 seeded per lens, so a pack's budget of 4 can reach recall 1.

items.why: toCsv already writes orders as CSV but only the nightly finance job calls it; SHOP-101, SHOP-104 and SHOP-109 ask for an order export (SHOP-113 is SHOP-101's customer again) and goal G-1 names records for bookkeeping.
listOrders already takes a status filter, but the GET /orders route never passes one; SHOP-120, SHOP-124 and SHOP-127 ask to filter the order history by status.
Customers write to support to get a receipt resent (SHOP-131, SHOP-135, SHOP-138); resendReceipt does it in one call but only the admin CLI reaches it. Serves goal G-1.
An exported bulk function reached only from the admin CLI - but admin-only by design (its comment says prices never change from the storefront) and no ticket asks for it.
Looks like an internal helper with no route, but GET /search?suggest=1 already exposes it and docs/api.md documents it.
A declined card resets the checkout form and shows 'Something went wrong. Please try again later.' with no cause and no next step; SHOP-142 and SHOP-146 describe re-typing everything.
Subscribing is one click; cancelling is four steps with a fake countdown and a pre-ticked 'pause instead' box that turns a cancel into a pause (SHOP-150, SHOP-153).

Card logos without alt text (1.1.1), inputs with placeholders but no labels (1.3.1, 3.3.2), a pay control that is a div with onclick and an unlabelled icon (2.1.1, 4.1.2), a red dot as the only status (1.4.1); SHOP-157 and SHOP-158.
Save address fires a fetch and ignores the answer: no progress, no 'Address saved.' (the server sends it), no error for an incomplete address; SHOP-161 and SHOP-164.
An error path that does recover: the cart keeps its contents, the message says how to make room, and it links to the cart.
An empty state that offers two ways forward (show all products, search).
Looks like the checkout page's markup, but here the logo has alt text, the search input has a label and the icon button has aria-label.
The configuration guide documents MAX_CART_ITEMS default 50; src/config.js defaults to 20 since the commit that lowered the cart limit (SHOP-175).
The CLI guide (and Confluence PAGE-301) still tells owners to cron `pebble orders sync`; the command and src/jobs/orders-sync.js were removed in a commit 60 days ago (SHOP-172).
A commit 25 days ago added guest checkout behind PEBBLE_GUEST_CHECKOUT; no doc mentions the variable (SHOP-170 asks how to turn it on).
The POST /cart curl example sends `qty`; addToCart reads `quantity`, so the example silently adds 1 item instead of 2.
The README's claims hold: port 8080 by default, PORT overrides it, npm ci / npm start / npm test exist.
Mentions `pebble orders sync`, but as history: 1.3.0 added it and 1.4.0 records its removal. Not a ghost feature.
The resend command and its output match cli/pebble.js and resendReceipt exactly.
lodash is pinned at 4.17.15; the captured npm audit lists GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm (high, command injection via template) and GHSA-p6mc-m468-83gw (high); the runtime receipt mailer calls _.template.
The q query parameter is concatenated into a SELECT ... LIKE string; db.query runs it unparameterised.
A live StonePay merchant key (psk_live_...) is committed in src/config.js and sent as the bearer token on every charge.
The shop ships to self-hosting owners (README, release workflow), but there is no SECURITY.md, no security.txt and no disclosure contact anywhere.
Matches the secret grep (api_key = '...'), but it is a stand-in for a fake server in a unit test and opens nothing.
child_process.execFileSync with constant arguments (git rev-parse --short HEAD): a sink with no user input.
innerHTML is assigned a constant string; product data goes through createElement and textContent.
The release workflow already produces a CycloneDX SBOM and publishes it with each release.
Dependency update automation exists (weekly Dependabot for npm); releases are versioned tags. Not an update-path gap.
